::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

<!-- No caption here. This include is wrapped in a Quarto figure div in
     ch10-inversion-recovery.qmd, which supplies the caption so the figure
     is numbered and cross-referenceable like every other figure in the
     book. Adding a <p class="caption"> back would double it up. -->

<!-- This include loads no shared assets of its own. Its only consumer,
     chapters/ch10-inversion-recovery.qmd, has already pulled them in by the
     time it appears: figures.css, plotly-cartesian.min.js and qmrust_wasm.js
     from includes/fig-t1-equations.qmd, and data-t1map.js plus ir-shared.js
     from includes/fig-ir-mag-vs-signal.qmd. Order on the page is
     fig-t1-equations -> fig-ir-mag-vs-signal -> this one.
     Loading qmrust_wasm.js a second time is not merely wasteful: the file
     opens with a top-level `let wasm_bindgen`, and a redeclaration in the
     global lexical scope is a SyntaxError that kills the second script.
     If this figure is ever used on a page without those two includes, the
     asset tags have to come back. -->

<div class="qmrust-figure">

<p id="q-status" hidden style="font-size:12px;color:#a11;margin:0 0 10px"></p>

<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:nowrap;gap:16px;align-items:flex-start;overflow-x:auto">
  <div id="q-curves" style="flex:1 1 430px;min-width:400px"></div>
  <div id="q-maps"   style="flex:0 0 250px"></div>
</div>

<div style="margin:10px 0 0;max-width:660px">
  <label for="q-ti" style="font-size:13px">Inversion time TI = <b><span id="q-tival">1.00</span> s</b></label>
  <input id="q-ti" type="range" min="0.01" max="5" step="0.01" value="1" style="width:100%">
</div>


</div>

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var TNR = "Times New Roman";
  var CFGP = { showLink: false, displayModeBar: false, responsive: true };
  /* T1 recalibration, tissue list, qmrust wrappers and the grid/crop helpers
     all live in interactive/ir-shared.js, so this figure and the
     magnetization-vs-signal figure above it cannot disagree about which
     voxel is which tissue. */
  var TISSUES = IR.TISSUES;
  var recipe = IR.recipe, forward = IR.forward;
  var grid = IR.grid, linspace = IR.linspace, axis = IR.axis;

  var TI_MAX = 5, NTI = 400;            // TI samples for the drawn curves
  var NLUT = 150;                       // TI samples for the image lookup
  var NBIN = 100;                       // T1 bins for the image lookup
  var MODE = "magnitude";               // this figure shows |Mz| only

  var tiGrid  = linspace(0.001, TI_MAX, NTI);
  var lutTi   = linspace(0.001, TI_MAX, NLUT);
  var curves = {};      // mode -> [ [y per tissue], ... ]
  var lut = {};         // mode -> Float64Array(NBIN * NLUT)
  var t1Lo = 0.05, t1Hi = 5.0;

  /* ---- one-time Rust work -------------------------------------------------
     forward() takes a whole list of inversion times, so the entire TI axis for
     one T1 costs a single call. Precomputing a T1-bin x TI table here keeps the
     slider instant; per-voxel-per-TI calls would be ~16k per slider tick.

     The cost is essentially linear in NBIN x NLUT, because forward() hands its
     result back as JSON and the serialise/parse dominates. So the table gets a
     coarser TI axis than the curves do: the three curves are what the reader
     actually reads values off, and they are only three calls, so they keep the
     fine grid. The table only has to look right as a grayscale image, where
     NBIN sets how finely T1 is banded and NLUT how finely the slider steps. */
  function precompute() {
    [MODE].forEach(function (m) {
      var cfgCurves = recipe(tiGrid, m);
      curves[m] = TISSUES.map(function (t) { return forward(cfgCurves, t.T1, 1.0, -2.0); });
      var cfgLut = recipe(lutTi, m);
      var table = new Float64Array(NBIN * NLUT);
      for (var b = 0; b < NBIN; b++) {
        var T1 = t1Lo + (t1Hi - t1Lo) * (b + 0.5) / NBIN;
        var y = forward(cfgLut, T1, 1.0, -2.0);
        table.set(y, b * NLUT);
      }
      lut[m] = table;
    });
  }

  var map = null;
  function cropGrid(g) { return IR.cropGrid(g, map.bbox); }

  /** Synthetic IR image at one TI, read out of the precomputed Rust table. */
  function irImage(ti) {
    var k = Math.round((ti - lutTi[0]) / (lutTi[1] - lutTi[0]));
    k = Math.max(0, Math.min(NLUT - 1, k));
    var table = lut[MODE], out = new Array(map.T1map.length);
    for (var v = 0; v < map.T1map.length; v++) {
      if (!map.mask[v] || !Number.isFinite(map.T1map[v]) || map.T1map[v] <= 0) { out[v] = null; continue; }
      var b = Math.floor((map.T1map[v] - t1Lo) / (t1Hi - t1Lo) * NBIN);
      b = Math.max(0, Math.min(NBIN - 1, b));
      out[v] = table[b * NLUT + k];
    }
    return out;
  }

  function drawCurves(ti) {
    var traces = TISSUES.map(function (t, i) {
      var name = "T<sub>1</sub> = " + t.T1.toFixed(2) + " s (" + t.label + ")";
      return { x: tiGrid, y: curves[MODE][i], mode: "lines", name: name, text: name,
               hoverinfo: "x+y+text" };
    });
    var yTitle = "|M<sub>z</sub>|";
    Plotly.react("q-curves", traces, {
      width: 430, height: 330, margin: { l: 55, r: 8, b: 50, t: 10 },
      xaxis: axis({ title: { text: "Inversion Time – TI (s)", font: { family: TNR, size: 15 } } }),
      yaxis: axis({ title: { text: yTitle, font: { family: TNR, size: 15 } },
                    range: [0, 1.05] }),
      // About as low as it goes: the CSF curve's right-hand tail reaches
      // |Mz| = 0.43 at TI = 5 s, which is y = 0.41 on this axis.
      legend: { x: 1, y: 0.41, xanchor: "right", yanchor: "bottom",
                font: { family: TNR, size: 11 }, bgcolor: "rgba(255,255,255,0.75)" },
      shapes: [{ type: "line", x0: ti, x1: ti, yref: "paper", y0: 0, y1: 1,
                 line: { color: "#444", width: 1.5, dash: "dot" } }],
      plot_bgcolor: "white", paper_bgcolor: "white"
    }, CFGP);
  }

  function drawMaps(ti) {
    var blank = { showgrid: false, zeroline: false, showticklabels: false, ticks: "" };
    // The T1 map supplies the per-voxel T1 the inversion-recovery image is
    // computed from; it is not itself displayed.
    var traces = [
      { type: "heatmap", z: cropGrid(grid(irImage(ti), map.nx, map.ny, 0, 1)),
        colorscale: [[0, "rgb(0,0,0)"], [1, "rgb(255,255,255)"]],
        zmin: 0, zmax: 1,
        colorbar: { title: { text: "|S|", side: "top", font: { family: TNR, size: 13 } },
                    thickness: 7, len: 0.72 },
        hovertemplate: "|S| = %{z:.2f}<extra></extra>" }
    ];
    Plotly.react("q-maps", traces, {
      width: 250, height: 330, margin: { t: 30, r: 2, b: 6, l: 2 },
      annotations: [
        { text: "IR image at TI = " + ti.toFixed(2) + " s", x: 0.5, y: 1.10,
          xref: "paper", yref: "paper", showarrow: false,
          font: { family: TNR, size: 15 } }
      ],
      xaxis: Object.assign({ domain: [0, 0.88] }, blank),
      yaxis: Object.assign({ domain: [0, 1], scaleanchor: "x" }, blank),
      plot_bgcolor: "white", paper_bgcolor: "white"
    }, CFGP);
  }

  function redraw() {
    var ti = parseFloat($("q-ti").value);
    $("q-tival").textContent = ti.toFixed(2);
    drawCurves(ti);
    drawMaps(ti);
  }

  /* The status paragraph stays hidden on the happy path -- progress and timing
     chatter is developer interest, not something a reader of the book needs.
     It is only revealed when the figure cannot be drawn, so a failure explains
     itself instead of leaving an empty box. */
  function fail(msg, e) {
    var el = $("q-status");
    el.textContent = msg;
    el.hidden = false;
    if (e) { console.error(e); }
  }

  window.addEventListener("load", function () {
    if (typeof Plotly === "undefined") { fail("Plotly failed to load."); return; }
    wasm_bindgen({ module_or_path: "interactive/qmrust_wasm_bg.wasm" }).then(function () {
      setTimeout(function () {
        precompute();
        setTimeout(function () {
          map = IR.loadT1Map();
          redraw();
          $("q-ti").addEventListener("input", redraw);
        }, 20);
      }, 20);
    }).catch(function (e) {
      fail("qMRust failed to start: " + e, e);
    });
  });
})();
</script>

:::
